item: launch.sh writes a stop-asked row before forwarding or waiting; the next boot reads it as a stop requested, never a crash
summary: On INT, TERM or HUP the launcher appends one row (signal name, server pid, time, boot id; nothing from the environment) to launcher_stops.jsonl before it forwards anything. An unclean end with that row reads as stop requested, teardown incomplete; with no row it keeps the old cannot-be-told wording. The stop block (307 B widest, measured) takes the slot of the exit block (384 B widest) because a session has one or the other. Bare kill -INT on the launcher stays a named residual.
